validity.recommendation: keep as operating; existence, classification, and non-duplicate status are all confirmed independent of GEM/wiki -- see the attribution/spec concerns below for the specific corrections owed
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED independent of GEM/wiki: Ozark Gas Transmission, L.L.C. is an active FERC-regulated interstate pipeline that filed a routine Annual Fuel Use Report for 2025 on 2026-03-31 under Docket RP26-712-000 (federalregister.gov Combined Notice of Filings, 2026-04-06) and has an open, actively-worked expansion docket, CP22-511-000 (filed 2022-09-19, still receiving weekly status reports as of late 2023 per search results), for its 'Supply Access' project -- 2.0 miles of 16-inch loop pipe, a new 5,000 hp compressor station, and two new receipt-point interconnects in Lawrence and Izard Counties, Arkansas, under Ozark's blanket certificate CP91-945-000. CLASSIFICATION CONFIRMED as interstate gas TRANSMISSION (not gathering): IREI (irei.com, independent real-estate/infrastructure trade press) explicitly distinguishes the company's two Ozark-branded assets acquired from Enbridge in April 2020 -- 'OGT' (Ozark Gas Transmission, this row, a '367-mile, interstate natural gas pipeline transportation system') and 'OGG' (Ozark Gas Gathering, a separate 'fee-based, 330-mile natural gas gathering system that connects regional production into OGT's pipeline'). A second independent source, World Pipelines (worldpipelines.com, 2020-10-01), confirms Black Bear Transmission SOLD the OGG gathering assets only months after acquiring them ('Black Bear Transmission Sells Ozark Natural Gas Gathering Assets') -- i.e. the gathering system left Black Bear's portfolio entirely in late 2020, while OGT (this row) was retained and remains FERC-regulated transmission today, per Ozark's own current asset page (blackbearllc.com/ozark-gas-transmission) and the two active FERC dockets cited above. NO DUPLICATE against the Black Bear Transmission cluster (P0185 AlaTenn, a physically separate Tennessee/Alabama system) or against any gathering-system row -- OGG is not tracked by this batch and, per the 2020 divestiture, is no longer a Black Bear/Ozark asset at all.

The sheet's EndState/Province='Missouri' is therefore CORRECT; the row's mapped route geometry ending short (in Arkansas) is consistent with the row's own recorded RouteAccuracy='low' and is a geometry-completeness issue, not a data-value error. validity.recommendation: keep LengthKnown=589 km as recorded -- confirmed within rounding by two independent current sources -- but note the much larger 455-mile figure in the original 1981 FERC certificate as a historical caveat
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's recorded 589 km (~366 mi) is confirmed within rounding by two independent CURRENT sources: the operator's own asset page (blackbearllc.com/ozark-gas-transmission, '368 miles from Latimer County, OK to Dunklin County, MO' = 592.2 km, a 0.5% delta) and Rextag's independent database (rextag.com/pages/ozark-gas-transmission, 'Miles of Pipeline: 367' = 590.6 km, a 0.3% delta). However, a THIRD source -- a contemporary Energy Law Journal committee report on the original certification (eba-net.org, 'Report of the Committee on Natural Gas Certificate and Authorization,' covering 1981 FERC decisions) -- states FERC's Opinion No. 125 (issued 1981-07-28, Docket CP78-532) 'granted certification for the proposed construction and operation of a 455 mile pipeline project.' This is nearly 90 miles longer than the two current figures. Recommend NOT changing the recorded value (the two current, independent, operator/vendor sources agree closely with it), but flagging the original certificate's larger scope as a documented historical caveat -- the as-certified 1978/1981 project apparently was not built to its full authorized length, or the 455-mile figure included laterals/looping not present in the current mainline mileage count; no source found resolves which.
